author: OriginalRoddick
text: California’s reporting of murder rates to the FBI and other agencies has faced scrutiny due to inconsistencies and incomplete data, particularly since the FBI’s 2021 transition to the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS). That year, only 2% of California agencies submitted data, leaving significant gaps that required FBI estimates, which can introduce inaccuracies. While reporting improved by 2023, some, like San Jose and San Bernardino, still failed to submit data for certain periods, and others, like Oakland, required corrections for errors. Potential misclassification of crimes and allegations of underreporting to downplay violent crime further cloud reliability, though such claims lack conclusive evidence. Cross-referencing FBI data with California DOJ and local police reports is recommended, but even these may not fully capture the true murder rate due to systemic reporting challenges.

text:
The 2021 NIBRS participation data to identify the states that do not report crime to the FBI. In each of the 21 states on this list, at least a third of law enforcement agencies did not submit crime data to the FBI in 2021.

Due to low participation, critical measures such as the homicide rate and the overall violent crime rate are missing in nine of the states on this list.
